keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Oettingen row). The page: 'At the end of the Old Kingdom in 1806, the area covered around 850 km2 (330 sq mi) and had around 60,000 inhabitants'; before that 'From the 12th to the 14th century the family gained the largest secular territory in East Swabia'. A 16.4 km circle at 10.55E 48.90N (850 km2) is a soft stand-in for the 1806 figure and is too small for the earlier county.

ledger.note: About 1147 (page silent on a founding date; 'The Oettingen family was first mentioned in 1147 with Ludovicus comes de Otingen, who was granted the county surrounding the Imperial city of Nördlingen as a fief' - the year is that of the first mention, 'First documentary mention: 1147').

1522: the partition. Infobox 'Partitioned to Ö-Oettingen and Ö-Wallerstein: 1522' (earlier partitions: 1418, 1442, 1485; later: Spielberg 1602, Baldern 1623). Entered as a dynastic step inside one state (rule 2); the page's own dates for the first Wallerstein partition differ (1418, 1423).

1674: princes. 'In 1674 the house was raised to the rank of prince for the first time.' (A line 'created Prince of the Holy Roman Empire in 1674 but became extinct in 1731'; the principality is dated 1734 and 1774 in other lines.)

1806: mediatised. 'In 1806, it was mediatised to the Kingdom of Bavaria, and divided with the Kingdom of Württemberg in 1810.' 'At this time, the Principality had a territory of 850 km2 (330 sq mi) with 60,000 inhabitants.'

certainty.note: The page gives only the 1806 area (850 km2); the circle is a stand-in, too small for the larger medieval county.

notes:
Written 2026-10-25 for batch eu-09-x (1 page; budget 1-2). New state: Cliopatria has no Oettingen row.

SCOPE. The page covers a family and its partitions (Oettingen-Oettingen, -Wallerstein, -Spielberg, -Baldern, -Katzenstein); they are kept inside one state (rule 2). The start year 1147 is the first documentary mention, confidence 1. The page is silent on wars. The imperial ban of May 1310 against a count over a dispute with the Prince-Bishopric of Eichstatt ('which stripped him of his property') names no land and is not entered.

SHAPES. A single circle at 10.55E 48.90N, 16.4 km (850 km2) for 1806; The gazetteer has neither Oettingen nor Nördlingen, hence the coordinate circle. Gazetteer names wanted: 'Oettingen in Bayern', 'Nördlingen', 'Wallerstein', 'Harburg', 'Spielberg'.

NOT SETTLED. (1) No early area; (2) the page's dates conflict: Wallerstein 1418 or 1423, Baldern extinct 1789 (text) or 1798 (infobox), the principality 1674, 1734 or 1774; (3) the 1810 split with Württemberg; (4) who held the lands in the 13th and 14th centuries beyond 'the largest secular territory in East Swabia'.
